title: Easy Cheesy Beef Taco Rice Skillet (One-Pan Family Dinner)
contentHtml:
This easy cheesy beef taco rice skillet gives you taco-night flavor in one pan with ground beef, rice, black beans, corn, tomatoes, and plenty of melted cheese. It is filling, beginner-friendly, and built for nights when you want a real family dinner without creating a sink full of dishes.

The best part is that the rice cooks right in the skillet with the seasoned beef. Add the toppings you like, skip the ones you do not, and dinner is handled.

Easy Cheesy Beef Taco Rice Skillet Recipe

Prep time: 10 minutes
Cook time: 30 minutes
Total time: 40 minutes
Yield: 6 servings

Equipment

  • Large 12-inch skillet with a lid
  • Wooden spoon or sturdy spatula
  • Cutting board and knife
  • Measuring cups and spoons

Ingredients

  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 pound lean ground beef
  • 1 small yellow onion, diced
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tablespoons taco seasoning
  • 1 cup long-grain white rice, uncooked
  • 1 can diced tomatoes with juices, 14.5 ounces
  • 1 1/2 cups low-sodium beef broth
  • 1 can black beans, 15 ounces, drained and rinsed
  • 1 cup corn, frozen or drained canned corn
  • 1 cup salsa
  • 1 1/2 cups shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese
  • 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 jalapeno, thinly sliced, optional
  • 1/2 cup diced fresh tomato or pico de gallo, optional
  • 1/4 cup diced red onion, optional
  • 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, optional
  • 1/2 cup sour cream, optional for serving
  • 1 lime, cut into wedges, optional for serving

Instructions

  1. Brown the beef. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and onion. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking the beef into crumbles, until no pink remains and the onion is softened. Ground beef should reach 160°F. Drain excess grease if needed.
  2. Add the seasoning. Stir in the garlic and taco seasoning. Cook for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
  3. Build the skillet. Stir in the uncooked rice, diced tomatoes with their juices, beef broth, black beans, corn, salsa, salt, and black pepper. Scrape the bottom of the skillet so nothing is stuck underneath.
  4. Simmer. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover. Cook for 18 to 20 minutes, or until the rice is tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed. Avoid lifting the lid repeatedly because the trapped steam helps cook the rice.
  5. Check the rice. If the rice is still firm but the pan looks dry, add 2 to 4 tablespoons of broth or water, cover again, and cook another 3 to 5 minutes.
  6. Add the cheese. Sprinkle the cheese evenly over the top. Cover for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cheese is fully melted.
  7. Finish and serve. Remove from the heat and let the skillet stand for 5 minutes. Top with jalapeno, fresh tomato or pico de gallo, red onion, cilantro, and sour cream if using. Serve with lime wedges.

Useful Cooking Tips

  • Use regular long-grain white rice. Instant rice and brown rice need different liquid ratios and cooking times.
  • Keep the simmer low. A hard boil can cook off the broth before the rice has time to soften.
  • Drain very fatty beef. Too much grease can make the finished skillet heavy instead of cheesy and saucy.
  • Let it rest. Five minutes off the heat gives the rice time to finish absorbing moisture and makes the skillet easier to serve.

Easy Substitutions

  • Ground beef: Use ground turkey or ground chicken. Cook poultry to 165°F.
  • Beans: Pinto beans work just as well as black beans.
  • Cheese: Cheddar, Monterey Jack, pepper Jack, or a Mexican-style blend all melt well.
  • Heat level: Use mild salsa and skip the jalapeno for kids, or use hot salsa and pepper Jack for more heat.
  • Vegetables: Add a diced bell pepper with the onion or stir in chopped spinach during the last few minutes.

What to Serve With Taco Rice Skillet

This is already a complete meal, but tortilla chips, a simple green salad, sliced avocado, or extra salsa all work well on the side. If you are feeding a bigger crew, warm tortillas make it easy to turn the skillet into quick burritos.

Storage and Reheating

Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate them in an airtight container for up to 3 to 4 days. Reheat individual portions in the microwave with a tablespoon of water or broth stirred in to keep the rice from drying out. For a larger amount, reheat covered in a skillet over low heat until steaming hot throughout.

You can freeze the cooled beef-and-rice mixture for up to 2 months. For the best texture, add fresh toppings and sour cream only after reheating.

Estimated Nutrition

Estimated per serving before optional sour cream and toppings: about 520 calories, 28g protein, 55g carbohydrates, 21g fat, and 9g fiber. Actual nutrition varies with the beef, cheese, salsa, and serving size used.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I make taco rice skillet ahead of time?

Yes. Cook the full skillet, cool it, and refrigerate it. Reheat with a splash of broth or water, then add fresh toppings right before serving.

Why is my rice still crunchy?

The skillet may have cooked too hot or lost too much steam. Add a small splash of broth or water, cover tightly, and continue cooking over low heat for a few more minutes.

Can I use brown rice?

Brown rice needs more liquid and a longer cooking time, so it is not a direct one-for-one swap in this version. For the most reliable result, use long-grain white rice.
